$comment: The accepted npm-audit findings for site/, recorded explicitly so a NEW finding is
distinguishable from the set already reasoned about (#56, #59). scripts/check-npm-audit.mjs
compares `npm audit --omit=dev --json` against this file. It runs REPORT-ONLY in CI today:
an audit goes red because the world changed, not because someone changed the code, and a
guard that stops unrelated merges gets suppressed (which is how audits stop meaning
anything). The graduation path is in #59: report first, then fail on a DELTA against this
baseline. Adding an entry here is an explicit act of acceptance, not a suppression file.
REACHABILITY. `site/package.json` declares 13 dependencies and no devDependencies, so
`--omit=dev` excludes nothing: every finding below is a production dependency of the built
site. The accepted set is reachable only through `firebase`, and the site uses firebase's
browser Auth SDK on the sign-in page. The condition that keeps this acceptable is:
static build, no SSR, no Node server runtime, and no Firestore/gRPC calls at build or
request time. If that stops being true, these findings become reachable and this baseline

accepted.summary: getAuthContext can return unauthorized certificates as though they were authorized
accepted.reason: No patched version is reachable: firebase@12.19.0 (latest) still resolves @grpc/grpc-js <=1.13.5, and `npm audit fix --force` proposes a DOWNGRADE to firebase@9.14.0. The vulnerable code is the gRPC transport, which the browser Auth SDK does not use.

accepted.summary: The server transmits some error messages thrown by method handlers to the client in status messages
accepted.reason: Same dependency and path as the other @grpc/grpc-js advisory; only a gRPC server is affected, and the hub runs no gRPC server.
